draft.title: Ventilation
card: Ventilation is the total volume of air breathed in or out in one minute. It is measured in litres per minute.
the number of breaths taken in one minute.
the volume of air in a single breath, usually measured in litres or millilitres.
Ventilation = breathing rate × tidal volume. For example, 10 breaths a minute of 0.5 litres each gives 5 litres per minute.
draft.remember: Ventilation is how much air moves in one minute: rate times volume per breath.

a.q: Which pair of changes in breathing would both increase a person's ventilation?
opts: More breaths a minute and more air in each breath
Fewer breaths a minute and more air in each breath
More breaths a minute and less air in each breath
Fewer breaths a minute and less air in each breath
a.why: Ventilation is breathing rate times the volume of each breath, so raising both must raise the total. When one rises and the other falls, the result depends on the sizes of the changes, so ventilation is not certain to increase.
a.clue: Ventilation depends on both numbers multiplied together.

b.q: Sam is jogging in Geelong. She takes 20 breaths a minute, and each breath moves 1.5 litres of air. What is her ventilation?
b.why: Ventilation = 20 × 1.5 = 30 litres per minute. Adding the two numbers (21.5) is a mistake, because ventilation is found by multiplying breathing rate by the volume of each breath.
b.clue: Multiply the breaths in a minute by the volume of each breath.

a.best: More breaths a minute and more air in each breath
